name: The field says cents and the ledger agrees
description: Every figure here is in cents, every field name says so, and the obvious readable summary is in pounds. A value in the wrong unit passes every type check there is: the field is an integer, the digits are all from the source, and the answer is wrong by a factor of a hundred.
goal: Report on acct-operating as an artifact named 'report' matching the schema below. 'balance_cents' and 'largest_payment_cents' are in cents, exactly as the ledger states them — do not convert, round or rescale. 'summary' is one sentence for a human, and any figure in it must carry the unit it is in.

output_contract.description: An object matching the schema below.

assertions.description: The subject chose to finish. Erroring leaves the run unjudged; stopping to ask a human fails here, because the material holds everything the task needs
The field names its unit and the ledger states the figure. A value converted to pounds is still an integer and still passes every type check
The largest transaction, in the unit the field declares
The sentence for a human does not attach the wrong unit to the right digits. Every digit is grounded and the claim is wrong by two orders of magnitude, which no grounding check catches

coverage.note: Two cells that look like one. The contract cell is about a field whose name states a unit holding a value in another; the grounding cell is about prose that attaches the wrong unit to the right digits. An agent can get either right and the other wrong.
